references.text: Moses further explains why the people come to him—to gain knowledge of God's statutes and laws
Moses brought the case of Zelophehad's daughters before the Lord, an example of seeking God for decisions
Rebekah went to seek the Lord (לִדְרֹשׁ) when she was troubled, using the same expression found here
In Israel, people said 'let us go to the seer' when they wanted to seek God, illustrating the practice of approaching a man of God for guidance
King Jehoshaphat asked to receive the Lord's word through a prophet, reflecting the same practice of seeking God through an intermediary
King Josiah sent people to seek the Lord regarding the book of the law that had been found
Ezekiel mentions that the elders of Israel came to seek the Lord through the prophet
Instructions to go to priests and judges when cases are too difficult establish the system for seeking God's judgment
Demonstrates Moses' role as a prophetic intermediary: 18:15 describes the function generally, while 9:8 shows it in practical action.
